47139-stories-from-wagner.title: From Wagner*
47139-stories-from-wagner.creator: Unknown
47139-stories-from-wagner.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. It would be a longer story than all the "Stories from Wagner" put together, to tell where these tales began and how they grew. Centuries before they were set to music in the soul of Richard Wagner, some of them had been chanted around rude camp-fires by savage-looking men clad in the skins of animals.

arxiv-2008-12995.title: AKHCRNet: Bengali handwritten character recognition using deep learning
arxiv-2008-12995.creator: Roy, Akash
arxiv-2008-12995.description: Abstract I propose a state of the art deep neural architectural solution for handwritten character recognition for Bengali alphabets, compound characters as well as numerical digits that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy 96.8% in just 11 epochs. Similar work has been done before by Chatterjee, Swagato, et al. [ 1 ] but they achieved 96.12% accuracy in about 47 epochs.

arxiv-2207-11252.title: Path integral molecular dynamics for anyons, bosons and fermions
arxiv-2207-11252.creator: Yunuo Xiong, Hongwei Xiong
arxiv-2207-11252.description: Abstract In this article we develop a general method to numerically calculate physical properties for a system of anyons with path integral molecular dynamics. We provide a unified method to calculate the thermodynamics of identical bosons, fermions and anyons. Our method is tested and applied to systems of anyons, bosons and fermions in a two-dimensional harmonic trap.

arxiv-2310-08699.title: CoLadder: Supporting Programmers with Hierarchical Code Generation in Multi-Level Abstraction
arxiv-2310-08699.creator: Ryan Yen, Jiawen Zhu, Sangho Suh, Haijun Xia, Jian Zhao
arxiv-2310-08699.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ryan Yen, Jiawen Zhu, Sangho Suh, Haijun Xia, Jian Zhao. Programmers increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) for code generation. However, misalignment between programmers’ goals and generated code complicates the code evaluation process and demands frequent switching between prompt authoring and code evaluation. Yet, current LLM-driven code assistants lack sufficient scaffolding to help programmers format intentions from their overarching goals, a crucial step before translating these intentions into natural language prompts.

arxiv-2404-07034.title: Quantum Tunneling: From Theory to Error-Mitigated Quantum Simulation
arxiv-2404-07034.creator: Sorana Catrina, Alexandra Băicoianu
arxiv-2404-07034.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sorana Catrina, Alexandra Băicoianu. 1
Abstract

Ever since the discussions about a possible quantum computer arised, quantum simulations have been at the forefront of possible utilities and the task of quantum simulations is one that promises quantum advantage. In recent years, simulations of large molecules through VQE or dynamics of many-body spin Hamiltonians may be possible, and even able to achieve useful results with the use of error mitigation techniques.

arxiv-2404-10063.title: Adjusting for bias due to measurement error in functional quantile regression models with error-prone functional and scalar covariates
arxiv-2404-10063.creator: Xiwei Chen a , Yuanyuan Luan a , Roger S. Zoh a , Lan Xue b , Sneha Jadhav c , and Carmen D. Tekwe a
arxiv-2404-10063.description: Abstract Wearable devices enable the continuous monitoring of physical activity (PA) but generate complex functional data with poorly characterized errors. Most work on functional data views the data as smooth, latent curves obtained at discrete time intervals with some random noise with mean zero and constant variance. Viewing this noise as homoscedastic and independent ignores potential serial correlations.

arxiv-2405-07097.title: Diffusion models as probabilistic neural operators for recovering unobserved states of dynamical systems
arxiv-2405-07097.description: Abstract This paper explores the efficacy of diffusion-based generative models as neural operators for partial differential equations (PDEs). Neural operators are neural networks that learn a mapping from the parameter space to the solution space of PDEs from data, and they can also solve the inverse problem of estimating the parameter from the solution.

arxiv-2501-04282.title: Combinatorial construction of symplectic 6-manifolds via bifibration structures Thanks: The author was supported by Japanese Society for the Promotion of Science KAKENHI Grant Numbers JP22K03320 and JP23K03123.
arxiv-2501-04282.creator: Kenta Hayano
arxiv-2501-04282.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kenta Hayano. A bifibration structure on a 6 6 -manifold is a map to either the complex projective plane ℙ 2 \mathbb{P}^{2} or a ℙ 1 \mathbb{P}^{1} -bundle over ℙ 1 \mathbb{P}^{1} , such that its composition with the projection to ℙ 1 \mathbb{P}^{1} is a ( 6 6 -dimensional) Lefschetz fibration/pencil, and its restriction to the preimage of a generic ℙ 1 \mathbb{P}^{1} -fiber is also a ( 4 4 -dimensional) Lefschetz fibration/pencil.

arxiv-2504-02111.title: Exploring LLM Reasoning Through Controlled Prompt Variations
arxiv-2504-02111.creator: Giannis Chatziveroglou MIT gchatz@mit.edu & Richard Yun MIT ryun@mit.edu & Maura Kelleher MIT maurakel@mit.edu
arxiv-2504-02111.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Giannis Chatziveroglou MIT gchatz@mit.edu & Richard Yun MIT ryun@mit.edu & Maura Kelleher MIT maurakel@mit.edu. This study investigates the reasoning robustness of large language models (LLMs) on mathematical problem-solving tasks under systematically introduced input perturbations. Using the GSM8K dataset as a controlled testbed, we evaluate how well state-of-the-art models maintain logical consistency and correctness when confronted with four categories of prompt perturbations: irrelevant context, pathological instructions, factually relevant but non-essential context, and a combination of the latter two.

pmc-11606126.title: Aquatic therapy for spastic cerebral palsy: a scoping review
pmc-11606126.creator: Aomeng Xiang, Yanxin Fu, Chengshuo Wang, Dan Huang, Jingman Qi, Ruoxuan Zhao, Liang Wu, Chunliang Fan, Qin Zhang
pmc-11606126.description: BackgroundCerebral palsy (CP) is a group of dysfunction syndrome. Spastic CP is the most common form of CP. As a specific treatment, aquatic therapy (AT) can improve spasticity, increase range of motion, and increase muscle strength due to its particular properties.ObjectivesThis article aims to review the research status of AT in patients with spastic CP.

pmc-11607154.title: The Role of Osteocalcin in Patients with Osteoporosis: A Systematic Review
pmc-11607154.creator: Seyed Mohammad Mohammadi, Nadia Saniee, Sajedeh Mousaviasl, Esmat Radmanesh, Amir Hossein Doustimotlagh
pmc-11607154.description: Background:Osteoporosis is the most common systemic skeletal disease worldwide. We aimed to review the latest studies related to osteocalcin and osteoporosis to clarify this relationship more precisely.Methods:A systematic literature search was performed to review studies on the effects of osteocalcin on osteoporosis, on studied published between January 2013 and January 2023.

pmc-12612087.title: Evaluating the impact of pre-slaughter transport stress on broiler welfare and meat quality in India
pmc-12612087.creator: Siddharth Mohan, Monika Madheshwaran, Akhilesh Kumar, Gopi Mariappan, Ashim Kumar Biswas, Jaydip Jaywant Rokade, Sonale Nagesh, Ashok Kumar Tiwari, Yazavinder Singh
pmc-12612087.description: This study aimed to find the optimal transportation time for broilers under Indian conditions, as transport duration significantly impacts their well-being and meat quality. An experiment involved 120 marketable birds, each marked with four distinct colors for identifying treatment groups.

pmc-12661463.title: Effect of Nutrition Interventions on the Dietary Diversity Status Among Pregnant Women in Ethiopia: Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-12661463.creator: Mahider Awoke Belay, Mulat Belay Simegn, Samuel Dagne Chanie, Werkneh Melkie Tilahun, Yonatan Menber, Yosef Wasihun, Zenebe Abebe Gebreegziabher, Zewudu Andualem, Ayenew Takele Alemu, Azeb Geddif, Genet Gedamu Kassie, Kalkidan Worku Mitiku
pmc-12661463.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The government of Ethiopia recommends nutrition counseling throughout pregnancy for better consumption of diversified diets, because improving maternal nutrition is vital for the prevention of maternal and child mortality and morbidity. As a result, the purpose of this study aimed to summarize the national evidence on the effect of nutrition intervention on dietary diversity status among pregnant women in Ethiopia using a systematic review and meta‐analysis.

pmc-12714705.title: Real-time capture of domain movements during copper amine oxidase catalysis by mix-and-inject serial crystallography
pmc-12714705.creator: Takeshi Murakawa, Mamoru Suzuki, Kenji Fukui, Tetsuya Masuda, Eiichi Mizohata, Ikuko Miyahara, Ikuya Kurauchi, Taiki Murakami, Himawari Matsunaga, Yoshiki Montawa, Norie Nakajima, Toshinori Oozeki, Katsuki Sakai, Teikoku Son, Takehiro Higuchi, Tomoko Sunami, Tetsunari Kimura, Kensuke Tono, Tomoyuki
pmc-12714705.description: Protein dynamics play a crucial role in various physiological functions, including enzyme catalysis. To explore conformational changes during enzyme catalysis, we conduct mix-and-inject serial crystallography, an advanced technique to capture time-resolved protein structures in real time, using the microcrystals of bacterial copper amine oxidase containing a protein-derived quinone cofactor.

pmc-13105696.title: Trends in mortality, pathogen distribution, and antimicrobial resistance of peritoneal and intra-abdominal infections from 1990 to 2021: a cross-sectional analysis of the MICROBE database
pmc-13105696.creator: Qiancheng Xu, Yan Qian, Mengqi Guan, Min Liu, Shuoshuo Wei, Yingya Cao, Xiaogan Jiang, Weihua Lu, Lei Zha
pmc-13105696.description: Background:Peritoneal and intra-abdominal infections (IAIs) are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in surgical patients, with rising antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatening surgical safety. This study mapped global and regional patterns in IAI burden and resistant pathogens to inform evidence-based surgical practice.

pmc-13225523.title: Masticatory function, inflammation, and mortality after stroke: A prospective cohort study
pmc-13225523.creator: Wenshu Zhang, Yu Wang, Yuli Wu, Feiyu Chen, Xiaoping Liu
pmc-13225523.description: This study aimed to clarify the relationship between masticatory function and mortality (both all-cause and cardiovascular) in stroke patients and explore the potential mediating role of systemic inflammation. This study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles spanning 1999 to 2018, comprising 1708 participants aged 20 or older with a history of stroke.

pmc-13297179.title: A Node-Adaptive Feature Fusion Network for Drug–Target Interaction Prediction Based on Multi-View Graphs
pmc-13297179.creator: Lin Xie, Hongmei Xu, Pinglu Zhang, Jianshe Xiong, Jing Li
pmc-13297179.description: Existing drug–target interaction (DTI) prediction methods still face challenges caused by sparse interaction data, complex multi-source relationships, and imbalanced information contributions among different nodes. In this study, we propose NAFF-DTI, a node-level adaptive feature fusion network based on multi-view graphs.

pmc-13575989.title: BCG after trimodality therapy: managing non-muscle-invasive recurrence in the irradiated bladder
pmc-13575989.creator: Nicola Fazaa, Etan Eigner, Melissa Atallah, Yuval Shafran, Gilad Amiel, Azik Hoffman
pmc-13575989.description: Trimodality therapy (TMT) is an established bladder-preserving option for selected patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer, but non-muscle-invasive recurrence remains a clinically relevant challenge. The role of intravesical bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) after prior bladder-directed chemoradiation is uncertain because the available evidence is limited to small retrospective cohorts and indirect studies in previously irradiated bladders.
